China Trademark Law 2026 Revision: Old Rules vs New Rules Side by Side

China's 2026 Trademark Law takes effect on 1 January 2027. This hub page maps every change that affects foreign brand owners to its article number and to the action it requires.

At a Glance

Adopted on 26 June 2026 and effective 1 January 2027, the revised PRC Trademark Law is the first comprehensive rewrite since 1983. It expands from 8 chapters / 73 articles to 9 chapters / 87 articles, adds a dedicated chapter on conditions for registration, and shifts the system's centre of gravity from "who registered first" toward "who actually uses the mark in good faith".

For foreign brand owners, the revision is net positive on enforcement but raises the compliance bar on portfolio maintenance. Below is the clause-by-clause comparison; for the decision-oriented version, see What Foreign Brands Should Do Before 1 January 2027.

Old vs New: Side-by-Side Comparison

TopicUntil 31 Dec 2026 (2019 law)From 1 Jan 2027 (2026 law)
Opposition after publication3 months (Art. 33)2 months (Art. 36)
Refusal review15 days to request review (Art. 34)15 days; decision in 9 months, +3 extension (Art. 37)
Registrable signsWords, devices, letters, numerals, 3D, colour combinations, sounds (Art. 8)Same plus dynamic / motion marks (Art. 14)
Applications without intent to useBad-faith applications not intended for use rejected (Art. 4)Refusal where there is no intent to use and the filing clearly exceeds normal business needs; deception or other improper means prohibited (Art. 19)
Penalty for the applicantNo fine on the applicant in the statuteWarning + fine up to RMB 100,000 for bad-faith filing causing adverse effects (Art. 54)
Misleading use of a registered markNo dedicated penaltyUp to 5× illegal turnover / RMB 250,000; possible revocation (Art. 56)
Non-use cancellationAny party may apply after 3 consecutive years (Art. 49)Any party may apply and CNIPA may cancel on its own initiative (Art. 57)
Well-known marksCross-class protection for marks registered in China (Art. 13)Cross-class protection regardless of Chinese registration (Art. 21)
Recognition vs confirmation"Recognition" of well-known status"Confirmation", also available in unfair-competition proceedings (Art. 63)
Internet useNot expressly statedUse via information networks expressly covered (Art. 2)
One-year re-filing blockApplied after cancellation, invalidation or non-renewal (Art. 50)Narrowed to voluntary cancellation by the owner (Art. 49)
Trademark agenciesGeneral duties (Art. 68)Recordal, practitioner sign-off, conflict-of-interest and penalty rules (Arts. 65–68)
DamagesStatutory calculation rulesReasonable enforcement costs expressly included (Art. 77)

The 2026 law renumbers the entire statute, so older commentary citing 2019 article numbers is easy to misread. Always check which version an article number refers to.

Six Changes That Matter Most for Foreign Brands

1. A two-month opposition window compresses the whole response chain

Article 36 cuts the publication-based opposition period from three months to two. Detection, internal go/no-go approval, evidence collection, translation and local counsel instruction all have to fit into a shorter window. Brands that check the register occasionally will miss deadlines; a continuous watch programme becomes a requirement rather than a nice-to-have.

2. CNIPA can now cancel idle marks without a third-party request

Article 57 adds ex officio cancellation for marks unused for three consecutive years without justification. This is a double-edged sword: it is an effective weapon against squatters who never use their registrations, but it also exposes dormant defensive registrations held by legitimate foreign brands. Article 2's express recognition of internet use helps — dated e-commerce listings, social accounts and online advertising can form part of a use-evidence file.

3. Bad-faith filing is attacked at three levels

Article 19 refuses speculative applications, Article 54 adds a fine of up to RMB 100,000, and Articles 65–68 impose duties and penalties on the agencies that assist them. Article 36 also makes "filing by deception or other improper means" an independent ground for opposition at the publication stage, rather than something that could only be raised later in invalidation.

4. Dynamic marks become registrable

Article 14 adds dynamic signs and their combinations to the list of registrable marks. Animated logos, app loading sequences and UI transitions that previously relied on copyright or unfair-competition arguments can now be protected as trademarks. The draft Examination Guidelines specify an MP4 video (up to 20 MB) plus 3–9 JPEG still frames and a description of how the mark is used.

5. Unregistered well-known marks gain cross-class protection

Article 21 removes the requirement that a well-known mark be registered in China before it can block dissimilar goods or services. Article 63 also allows well-known status to be confirmed in unfair-competition proceedings. This is directly relevant to foreign brands whose reputation in China precedes their filing — though strong evidence of that reputation remains essential.

6. Misleading use and "心机商标" become a registrant's own risk

Article 56 targets marks used in ways that mislead the public about quality, origin, ingredients or process, with fines and possible revocation. International brands using claims such as "Swiss Made", "medical grade" or "eco-friendly" in Chinese packaging, listings and advertising should be able to substantiate them — including when a licensee or OEM partner applies the mark.

What the Draft Transition Measures Add

Draft articleRulePractical reading
Art. 1–2No retroactivity; substantive issues under the old law, procedural issues under the newPre-2027 applications decided on or after 1 Jan 2027 are handled under the new law; invalidation/cancellation of pre-2027 registrations keeps old substantive law
Art. 3Dynamic mark filing materialsMP4 ≤20 MB, 3–9 JPEG frames, evidence of acquired distinctiveness within 15 days if requested
Art. 4Opposition period determined by publication dateDomestic: Gazette publication date. International registration: WIPO publication date. Pre-2027 = 3 months; from 2027 = 2 months; no restart of a running clock
Art. 6–7Isolation period and ex officio cancellationLocal trademark authorities investigate idle marks and report upward through CNIPA
Art. 9–10New law prevails over the old Implementing Regulations; measures effective 1 Jan 2027Do not assume the current Regulations override the revised statute during the transition

Draft status. These measures were published for comment on 28 September 2026 with a 12 November 2026 deadline, together with a draft Examination and Review Guidelines. Verify the final text before relying on any transition rule in a live matter.

Your Action List

  • Before 1 January 2027: run the five-step pre-2027 portfolio audit and reconfigure your watch service for a 2-month window.
  • Check eligibility, documents and the local-agent requirement in Who Can Register a Trademark in China.
  • Review the current process and timeline in the Complete Guide and How Long It Takes.
  • Refresh rejection-risk assumptions against Common Reasons for Rejection — Article 19 adds a new refusal ground.
  • If a squatter is already registered, compare opposition, invalidation, negotiation and rebranding in What Happens If Someone Registers Your Trademark First.

Sources, Status and Caveats

  • Full text: Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China (2026 Revision), CNIPA, 26 June 2026.
  • Official summary: CNIPA, Main Contents of the Revision to the PRC Trademark Law, 10 July 2026.
  • Transition: CNIPA notice on the draft Measures for Handling Business Matters Following the Revised Trademark Law and draft Trademark Examination and Review Guidelines, 28 September 2026.
  • Effective date and chapter structure also confirmed by the National People's Congress and the Supreme People's Court's public reporting, July–August 2026.

Article numbers refer to the 2026 law unless marked otherwise. This page is general information, not legal advice. Last reviewed: 6 November 2026.
